subject: DPA/SCCs: Hosting surcharge & transfer-mitigation ask — MedCore procurement
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medcore.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medcore.com
Date: 2029-03-21T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: Initial DPA redlines and hosting surcharge question

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call this morning. We reviewed the DPA redlines your team sent and have two high-level asks before we can move to signature: 1) confirmation that Redwood will maintain Controller/Processor roles as currently drafted for our EU PII flows, and 2) an explicit callout about hosting surcharge for on-prem/VPC hosting we discussed — Procurement needs clear language and an expected cost delta.

Attached is our procurement worksheet and a marked-up DPA (MedCore_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). A couple of specific points from our legal: they want SCCs reference updated to the newest EC implementing decision and an explicit Transfer Impact Addendum for UK/EU customers.

Can your team confirm whether the SCCs annex we saw is compatible with the most recent decision, and whether Redwood can accept the limited Transfer Impact Addendum language in section 4? If not, what alternatives do you propose?

Also looping in Craig from our counsel (mc-legal) in case we need legal-to-legal redlines.

Thanks — appreciate a consolidated reply we can share with Procurement.

Best,
Olivia Park
Head of Vendor Procurement
MedCore Health

Attachments: MedCore_DPA_Redline_v1.docx, Procurement_Worksheet_MedCore.xlsx

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medcore.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and hosting surcharge question

Hi Olivia — thanks for the summary and the redlines. Quick responses below and a plan to resolve: 

- SCCs: The annex we shared references the EC Implementing Decision 2024/915 (latest published). I'll confirm the exact citation in the annex and push an update if there is any mismatch.
- Transfer Impact Addendum: Redwood can accept a narrowly scoped transfer-impact annex limited to (a) additional safeguards (encryption + contractual commitments) and (b) routing fallback to EU-only hosts for EU-data when technically feasible. We cannot accept language that requires wholesale data localization by default.
- Hosting surcharge: This is a commercial ask. Ben — can you outline typical surcharge bands for Private (VPC) and On-Prem footprints so we can give Procurement a concrete delta?

Plan: I'll pull legal (Laura) into a short legal sync to propose wording for the Transfer Impact Addendum we hinted at, and Ben will provide the surcharge ranges. After that, we can circulate a clean DPA redline and a one-page summary for Procurement.

Would you be available for a 30-minute legal + procurement call Thursday (Mar 23) at 09:00 PT?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Contracts Counsel — Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0122

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medcore.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-22T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and hosting surcharge question — surcharge bands

Hi Olivia / Stephanie — following up with the commercials you asked for. High-level surcharge guidance (ballpark ranges to use in Procurement worksheet):

- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, multi-tenant control plane): +8-12% unit cost depending on commitment term and region.
- Redwood Private (VPC-managed in customer cloud): +15-25% typical uplift due to isolated provisioning and Egress controls.
- On-prem packaged deployment (customer-managed infra): +25-40% and possible professional services fee for install and support.

Notes: These are ranges; we can commit to a firm number once we know region, instance type, and retention settings for KV cache. Lauren/Law? (cc: laura) — we usually include a short clause in the Order Form that references "hosting surcharge schedule" and points to an annex with explicit dollar / percentage values to avoid re-negotiating the DPA itself.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medcore.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-23T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and hosting surcharge question — legal suggested language

Hi all — I reviewed Olivia's redline and sketched proposed language for two items: (1) a constrained Transfer Impact Addendum and (2) an SCCs citation update. Key points below; I'll attach a clean redline to the Drive link.

1) Transfer Impact Addendum (proposal) — short summary:
- Purpose: document supplemental safeguards and routing preference for personal data of EU/UK data subjects.
- Scope: applies only where Customer directs Redwood to process EU/UK personal data and where Customer has completed onboarding questionnaire.
- Remedies: Redwood will implement technical safeguards (at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys where requested, PKI-based mutual TLS, and route preference to EU regions). Where routing to EU-only hosts is not technically feasible for particular workloads, Redwood will document the rationale and offer mitigation (e.g., enhanced logging + contractual commitments).

2) SCCs: update the header to reference the EC Implementing Decision 2024/915 and include a short migration timeline clause: "Parties agree to reasonably cooperate to update Annex X to reflect any future governmental decisions affecting SCCs applicability."

Open items for MedCore: 1) confirm you are okay with the limited scope (not a data-locality mandate), and 2) procurement confirm which hosting option and region you'll pick so we can lock the surcharge.

I uploaded a DPA redline: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MedCore-DPA (MedCore_DPA_Redline_v1.docx -> MedCore_DPA_Redline_v1_LB.docx).

If helpful, Rishi (cc for privacy) and I can do a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to close the open contractual language before the procurement call.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-24T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: FW: DPA redline — quick privacy signoff request

Rishi — forwarding the thread. Laura drafted a constrained Transfer Impact Addendum and updated the SCCs citation. Can you review the proposed mitigation language below and confirm whether Privacy is comfortable with: (a) allowing customer-managed KMS for EU data, and (b) including the "route preference" (non-binding but documented) clause? We want privacy to sign off before we present the clean DPA to MedCore.

Key excerpt from Laura's draft: "Where routing to EU-only hosts is not technically feasible, Redwood will document the operational constraints and apply compensating controls including: (i) customer-managed encryption keys, (ii) enhanced access logging retained 12 months, and (iii) contractual commitments restricting use by support personnel outside the EU."

Please reply with your signoff or suggested edits — target EOD Mar 25 so we can stay on Procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Stephanie

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-26T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — privacy signoff and commercial path

Stephanie / Laura — thanks for the draft and context. Privacy reviewed the excerpt and we are comfortable with the proposed constraints, subject to two small changes: 1) increase access log retention from 12 to 18 months for EU-data routing exceptions, and 2) tighten the support access clause to require JML-backed time-limited privileged sessions for any support access from non-EU locations.

Commercial: Ben, with those privacy controls we can accept the Transfer Impact Addendum as Laura proposed. Ben, please confirm the hosting option MedCore will select and include a firm surcharge figure in the Order Form annex. Once Ben provides the surcharge and MedCore confirms region / hosting choice, we can circulate a "clean DPA + Order Form annex" for signature.

Rishi Malhotra
Privacy Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference

Onward: I'll approve inclusion of the SCCs update referencing EC Implementing Decision 2024/915.
